overview: The Norman royal court in Sicily brought together craftspeople and traditions from Latin, Byzantine and Islamic settings. Palermo was the kingdom's capital.

items.text: The surviving ensemble includes royal palaces, churches, cathedrals and the Admiral's Bridge.
The Palatine Chapel, Zisa Palace and cathedrals at Cefalu and Monreale formed distinct settings for courtly and religious life.
Mosaics, cut-stone pavements, marquetry, sculpture and painting drew on different Mediterranean traditions.
This synthesis influenced architecture elsewhere around the medieval Mediterranean. Shared craftsmanship alone does not establish social equality among all communities.
